## Core Overview
- Primary purpose: Analyze the time complexity of recursive algorithms using asymptotic notation.
- Fundamental themes: Breaking down recursive structures, solving recurrence relations, and proving bounds using mathematical induction.

## Key Concepts & Theorems/Formulas
- Recurrence Relations: Equations that define a function in terms of smaller inputs, such as T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).
- Recurrence Tree Method:
  - Visualizing the work done at each level of recursion.
  - Calculating cost per level = (number of nodes at level) * (cost of work at that node).
  - Summing the costs across all levels from level 0 to height log_b(n).
  - Total Cost = Base work + Intermediate levels work + Leaf work.
- Substitution Method:
  - Step 1: Guess the solution form (e.g., O(n) or O(n log n)).
  - Step 2: Use mathematical induction to prove the guess is correct.
  - Step 3: Substitute the inductive hypothesis into the recurrence and verify constants.
- Master Theorem (Implicit tool for check): Used for recurrences of the form T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).

## Exam Takeaways
- Always state base cases clearly when setting up or solving recurrences (e.g., T(1) = O(1)).
- Be comfortable expanding summations derived from recurrence trees using geometric series formulas.
- When using the substitution method, do not forget to prove the base case alongside the inductive step.
- Watch out for floor and ceiling functions in recursive divisions, though they can usually be omitted for asymptotic analysis unless specified.
- Common bounds to memorize: O(n) for single reduction by constant, O(n log n) for divide-and-conquer balanced splitting, and O(2^n) for recursive branching without memoization.
